title: Fluoroquinolone as a named gyrase-class
dek: Wikipedia class node. Moxifloxacin/levofloxacin plates and gyrA QRDR stay where doses and alleles live.
story: Fluoroquinolone on Wikipedia is a broad antibacterial class targeting DNA gyrase/topoisomerase IV. TB programmes care about later-generation members (moxifloxacin, levofloxacin) already plated as named drugs.
Ciprofloxacin is a Wikipedia celebrity that WHO does not want as a TB backbone. Class pages will not always say that loudly.
gyrA/gyrB QRDR mutations are the shared resistance grammar (tb-gyr-qrdr). This card is the class name in the graph.
deep: Moxifloxacin versus levofloxacin choice is a WHO/pharmacology plate, not an encyclopedia poll.
QTc stories with BDQ/CFZ live on monitoring plates.
Do not treat veterinary FQ exposure folklore as a DST.
Xpert XDR's FQ targets are a cartridge plate.
